newsitem.title: GERMANY: German P&I club posts favourable 1996 loss record.
newsitem.headline: German P&I club posts favourable 1996 loss record.

text.p: Trampfahrt, the only German P&I Club, achieved an excellent net loss ratio of 48.7 percent in 1996, as it suffered no large losses, board member Ulrich Schittek said on Monday.
The mutual marine protection and indemnity (P&I) insurer lifted premium income slightly to 16.0 million marks from 15.7 million marks.

The club had at year-end 1996 a total of 380 ships insured, unchanged from the previous year. Due to the favourable loss development, premium levels had been cut by 2.5 percent in 1996. Schittek said that he expects further reductions.

More than half of the insured fleet consists of container ships with an average age of 5.7 years. "The average age on a global scale is 11.1 years," Schittek said. Due to its focus on container shipping, the Club was spared costly losses from tankers and ferries.
Trampfahrt cedes 38 percent of its premium income to reinsurers, mainly Munich Re, with smaller portions also going to Swiss Re.

"Until 1992, we ceded most business to the UK market," said Schittek. However, it then developed a model together with Munich Re offering owners a fixed premium, rather than the levy system used by most P&I Clubs, Schittek said.
One particular problem was that of stowaways -- the number doubled last year to 50 and Trampfahrt had to pay more than 250,000 marks in repatriation costs.
